# Composition rules — visual discipline, new sub-objects, anti-AI, motion

**Read this when** drafting a sub-object that isn't already in the kit,
or doing the final self-check before producing `deck_output`. SKILL.md
hands off the "what stays stable vs. what may move" detail to this
file.

Decks are always rendered in canonical DataArt brand — there is **no**
client brand overlay for decks. Brand-overlay rules live in
`agent/skills/digital-product-poc/` (which has its own brand-overlay
reference). See `agent/references/review-presentation.md § Decision
scoping by task_type`.

---

## 0. Visual discipline — hard rules every slide must obey

These rules are checked BEFORE anything in §§ 1–4 applies. They are
template-agnostic and content-agnostic — if a slide breaks one, the
slide is wrong, full stop. Each rule has a `Why:` so edge cases are
judgable instead of robotically applied.

1. **Titles must wrap inside their column / region — never `white-space:nowrap`.**
   No `.col-title`, `.slide-heading`, column heading, or other label
   may have `white-space:nowrap`. A long title must wrap onto multiple
   lines within its own column.
   _Why:_ `nowrap` lets long titles overflow physically into the next
   column, crashing through numbering, accents, and content. Wrapping
   makes the column slightly taller but never broken. This is the
   exact bug that produces visible title overflow.

2. **Max one hero illustration per slide.**
   "Hero illustration" = any image / SVG with one side ≥ 300 px that
   carries narrative meaning (not a logo, not a decorative gradient
   panel, not an icon < 64 px). Two heroes compete for attention;
   the eye doesn't know where to land.
   _Why:_ a deck slide is an argument with one point. Two illustrations
   without a defined composition role read as a gallery, not an
   argument — the kit's whole presentation-grade rhythm dissolves.

3. **Decorative gradient panels behind columns — uniform or absent.**
   If a slide carries > 1 decorative `.layer` gradient panel, every
   panel must share the same `top` AND the same `height` (so they read
   as one set), OR they must be part of a canonical multi-panel
   composition. Panel A at `top:0;height:1080px` next to
   panel B at `top:400;height:546.667px` is "I gave up arranging" — drop
   them all rather than ship.
   _Why:_ mismatched top/height = visual noise the viewer reads as
   chaos. The Figma originals are uniform when they exist; we lose
   that uniformity only by accident.

4. **Off-canvas elements are forbidden outside the canonical patterns.**
   No element may be positioned at `top: -<n>px` or otherwise extend
   off the 1920×1080 canvas, except:
   - **title-background corner / edge graphics on cover & divider slides**
     (positioned to bleed past an edge by design — the `bg-title-0N`
     vivid covers),
   - **footer row** (sits at `y985.333` by canonical position).
     Anything else off-canvas — a graphic peeking from `top:-266.667px` is the
     typical example — is the model "polishing" without a rule.
     _Why:_ off-canvas peek-in without a declared pattern looks like
     uncertainty hidden in HTML. If the bleed is intentional, name the
     pattern and put it in this rule list. If it isn't, drop it.

5. **Vivid title backgrounds & their corner graphics are title-only.**
   The vivid `bg-title-03/04/05` backgrounds (cover; final uses 03/05 only —
   **bg-title-04 is forbidden on the final slide**) and the
   muted `bg-title-01/02/06` divider backgrounds, plus any corner /
   edge graphics they carry, are reserved for title-type slides
   (cover, section divider, final). Putting them on a content slide
   reads as "I needed to fill space".
   _Why:_ title backgrounds signal "you are entering a section"; content
   slides should never re-trigger that signal — content slides use
   `bg-content-01…08` only.

6. **Max 2 decoration layers per non-cover content slide.**
   Count: one uniform panel set (= 1 layer of decoration) + one accent
   (= 1 more) = the cap. Three or more decorative layers behind
   content text → the slide is being over-decorated. Drop to two
   before declaring done.
   _Why:_ the kit's visual identity comes from typography and grid
   discipline, not from accumulating decoration. Hard cap prevents the
   accumulation drift that hit slide-07.

These six rules apply to every materialised slide and every new
template. The use-as-is slides (fast-facts, capabilities, partnerships,
microsoft, contacts) carry decoration as part of their canonical
composition — those compositions exist as wholes, not as rules to be
generalised.

### § 0.7 — Three-layer composition discipline

Each slide is the sum of exactly **one L1 background + at most one L2
structural decoration + 1–3 L3 content seasonings.** Picking
discipline:

- **L1 (background) — rhythm-based, not content-locked.** A deck
  declares its **background palette** at Step 5a of Workflow:
  - **Title backgrounds** by role-pool — `bg-title-03/04/05` (vivid)
    for **cover + final**; `bg-title-01/02/06` (muted) for **section
    dividers**, one per section; `bg-cover-light` for the two-logo
    cover; `statement.html` keeps `bg-title-06`.
  - **Content backgrounds** — pick **one `bg-content-0N`** (01–08) per
    section and reuse it on every content slide in that section, so a
    section reads as a unit.
    Every slide takes its background from this palette based on its role.
- **L2 (structural decoration) — selective per content pattern.**
  Divider rules, chapter-number, accent rule, tag chips. Pick at most
  one; prefer "none" when the content already carries weight.
- **L3 (content seasoning) — locked per content pattern.** Two slides
  of the same content type within one deck must have identical L3
  (matrix `references/kit-map.md` § 5b).

### § 0.8 — Zone-conflict check before any new sub-object

Before placing any new non-text element (custom illustration,
prototype mockup, chart, photo, persona group, badge cluster) on a
slide, **identify its target zone** per `references/canvas-zones.md
§ 1` and **check background / content occupancy** per `§ 2 occupancy
table` of that file:

- **Zone marked `·` (free):** add freely, subject to hero-illustration
  cap (§ 0.2) and decoration cap (§ 0.6).
- **Zone marked `partial`:** add allowed but position the element away
  from the background's painted edge.
- **Zone marked `■` (decorated by background or filled by content):**
  **conflict.** Resolve by (a) move the element to a free zone, (b) drop
  the element (the existing content already carries the visual weight
  here), or (c) re-pick the content background for the slide if the
  element is structurally essential (escalates — affects the deck's
  background palette pick in Step 5a).
- **Zone is `top-right-logo` or `footer`:** **never replace** —
  canonical positions per § 1 of `kit-map.md`.

Record the decision in `deck_output.new_objects_introduced[]` with
`target_zone: <zone-id>` and `zone_occupancy_check: passed |
resolved-via-relocation | resolved-via-drop`.

> _Why:_ without this check the model layers a large illustration over
> a column already filled with numbered cards — the exact "stacking an
> illustration on top of finished content" antipattern that produces
> visual clash. The check is one lookup in canvas-zones.md before any
> new `<img>` / sub-object insert, and it's deterministic.

---

**Per-deck cap on background variety:** content backgrounds are picked
**one per section** (not per slide). A typical 8–12 slide deck spanning
2–4 sections therefore uses **2–4 unique `bg-content-0N` classes
total**, plus its title-background pools. If a deck reaches a different
content background on nearly every slide, sections are probably
mis-assigned — collapse before shipping.

> _Why:_ without one-background-per-section, the model has two failure
> modes — (a) "use a different content background on every slide"
> producing a different surface on 12 slides ("overload"), or (b) "stay
> safe with one background everywhere" producing flat decks with no
> visual chapters. One content background per section gives the eye
> signposts: each section reads as a coherent unit, and the title
> backgrounds mark the boundaries between them.

**Layout variety across the deck (anti-monotony).** The per-section background
rule above keeps a section unified — it is NOT a licence to render every slide in
that section with the same template. When consecutive content slides share a
shape (a common case: several "value / benefits / impact" slides are each "a few
parallel points"), ROTATE the rendering — **never reuse the same content template
more than twice in a row.** Pull the wider palette into long text-only runs: an
image (`content-text-media` / `content-media`), a comparison
(`content-comparison`), a stat-led slide (`content-stats-map`), a different list
shape (`content-stacked-list` vs `content-icon-grid`), or a `quote`. See the
rotation menu in `kit-map.md § 7`. `verify-deck.sh` surfaces a layout-streak
(informational, never blocks) at > 2 identical content templates in a row.

> _Why:_ background consistency plus a deterministic content-shape chooser push
> the model toward one template repeated down a section — the "four identical
> icon grids" regression. Backgrounds signpost sections; varied layouts keep a
> section from reading as one slide cloned N times. The two rules are orthogonal:
> same background, rotating layout.

### § 0.9 — Column-title adaptive sizing (Part 20 revised)

In multi-column layouts, column-title font size adapts to title
length AND character count to prevent two failure modes:
(a) wrap-to-2-lines → vertical-overflow cascade (§ 0.8);
(b) single-word overflow into adjacent column (e.g. "Cross-functional"
at 60 px in a 426 px col exceeds col width).

**4-col layouts (templates 04, 07) — Part 26 tightened:**

- **Default `.col-title.is-snug` (40 px)** for any title ≥ 2 words OR
  > 14 characters. Most real-world 4-col titles trigger this — «Discovery
  > workshop» (2 words, 18 chars), «Sign-off & kickoff» (3 words, 19 chars).
- `.col-title.is-tight` (48 px) — single-word, ≤ 12 chars.
- `.txt-h1` (60 px) — single-word, ≤ 8 chars.

**3-col layouts (templates 08, etc.) — Part 26 tightened:**

- Default `.txt-h1` (60 px) for short titles.
- `.col-title.is-tight` (48 px) — when title ≥ 3 words OR > 15 chars.
- `.col-title.is-snug` (40 px) — when title ≥ 4 words OR > 18 chars.
  («A category, not a brand» — 5 words, 21 chars — falls here.)

**2-col layouts:**

- Default `.txt-h1` (60 px).
- `.col-title.is-tight` (48 px) — when title > 20 chars.

The `.col-title.is-tight` and `.col-title.is-snug` modifiers live in
`kit-corporate/shared/components.css`.

> _Why:_ a 4-col layout has ≈ 362 px text width per column. «Phase-1
> build» wraps to 2 lines at 60 px, pushing column content down by
> ~ 72 px → § 0.8 vertical-overflow on the next bullet. «Cross-functional»
> (16 chars, single word) at 60 px hits ~ 528 px → overflows into the
> next column even without wrapping. 48 px default + 40 px snug
> modifier prevents both.

### § 0.9b — Title-body coupling (Part 26)

Column content (eyebrow + title + body + bullets) MUST live INSIDE the
same `.col` flex container. Splitting title into one `.layer` and body
into a separate `.layer` with its own `top: <fixed>px` absolute position
decouples vertical positions — when the title wraps to 2-3 lines, body
stays put and they OVERLAP. This was the «A category, not a brand /
Logo is lowercase italic» overlap visible in the user's deck.

**Forbidden pattern:**

```html
<!-- WRONG: title and body in separate absolute layers -->
<div class="layer col-table" style="top: 320px;">
  <div class="col"><p class="col-title">A category, not a brand</p></div>
  <div class="col"><p class="col-title">A site, not a system</p></div>
</div>
<div class="layer" style="top: 533.333px; left: 144px; width: 2272px;">
  <p>Logo is lowercase italic — no proprietary letterform</p>
  <!-- … more body text … -->
</div>
```

**Correct pattern:** one `.col-table` layer, all column content inside
each `.col`:

```html
<div class="layer col-table" style="left:144px; top:320px; width:2272px;">
  <div class="col">
    <div class="col-eyebrow"><p class="col-num">01</p></div>
    <p class="col-title txt-h1 is-snug c-white">A category, not a brand</p>
    <ul class="col-list disc-list has-icons is-dot txt-body c-white">
      <li>Logo is lowercase italic — no proprietary letterform</li>
      <li>Eight destination categories competing in the same cyan</li>
      …
    </ul>
  </div>
  <!-- next col, same pattern -->
</div>
```

_Why:_ `.col` uses `display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 16` —
children stack vertically and adapt to title wrap-height naturally.
Absolute positioning bypasses flex; the body's `top: 533.333px` ignores how
tall the wrapped title became, and overlap is the predictable failure.

### § 0.9c — Title leading + title→body gap (Part 33)

A slide-level title (`.txt-h1` / `.txt-h2` / `.txt-hero`) followed
by a description (`.txt-body` / `.txt-body-lg`) MUST live inside a
`.title-stack` flex container.

**Correct pattern:**

```html
<div class="layer title-stack" style="left:144px; top:320px; width:2272px;">
  <p class="txt-h1 c-white">A category, not a brand</p>
  <p class="txt-body c-light-blue">
    The product positions itself somewhere between travel and lifestyle, refusing the single
    category that retail demands.
  </p>
</div>
```

`.title-stack` does three things:

1. **Snug leading on the title** — overrides the token's default
   1.2 to 1.08. The wrapper-scoped override means existing slides
   using `.txt-h1` outside `.title-stack` keep their current
   rhythm; only the new wrapper opts in.
2. **32-px margin-bottom between title and description.** The
   pair gets _less_ internal title air and _more_ between-element
   air, so the two read as a coupled unit rather than slipping
   together.
3. **`max-width: 100%`** on the body — body never escapes the
   container's width.

_Why the wrapper-scoped fix instead of changing
`kit-corporate/shared/tokens.css`:_ tightening `line-height` at the token
level would shift every existing kit template and produced
deck — a regression nobody asked for. The wrapper opts new
content into the corrected rhythm; legacy stays pixel-stable.

_Why 1.08 specifically:_ at 60-px font with letter-spacing
−0.6 px (the `.txt-h1` token), 1.08 puts ascender-to-descender
clearance at ~5 px — readable, not cramped — and the
between-line gap stops competing with the 32-px margin-bottom
for visual rhythm.

**Body length escape rule.** If the description copy would push
out of the visible canvas given the slide's edge padding,
SHORTEN the body or split the slide — `.title-stack` does **not**
enable overflow / scroll / clip. The wrapper guarantees
stack-fit; the agent guarantees copy-fits-canvas.

Verify-slide.sh § Title rhythm gate flags any `.txt-h1/h2/hero`
followed by `.txt-body/.txt-body-lg` in sibling DOM that isn't
inside a `.title-stack` wrapper.

### § 0.10 — Illustration-usage rule

After content placement on a slide, **check canvas zones for free
illustration opportunities**:

1. Read the slide's content background → look up free zones in
   `references/canvas-zones.md § 2 occupancy table`.
2. If a free zone is ≥ 300 px on at least one dimension AND no
   content occupies it → **consider** adding an illustration / icon
   from `kit-corporate/assets/` whose semantics fit the slide's argument.
3. Skip if no kit illustration semantically fits — never pad with
   random decoration just to fill space.

Heuristic by layout:

- `col-right` free in a 2-column split → illustration / visual on the
  right side (`content-split` pattern).
- A dedicated visual slot free → drop a map / chart / illustration in
  the `content-stats-map` right slot.
- All columns filled with `numbered-card` / `icon-block` → no
  illustration; the content already carries visual weight in every
  column.
- `content-team` / persona content → use the kit's photo / avatar
  components rather than adding a separate illustration.

> _Why:_ illustrations were appearing **opportunistically** in real
> decks — model adds an illustration when it «felt right», skipped
> when it didn't, with no rule. This made some slides feel poured-on
> and others empty. Linking illustration placement to canvas-zones
> free-zone discovery makes the choice deterministic: zone free → ask
> «does any kit asset semantically belong here»; if yes, add; if no,
> leave the zone clean.

### § 0.10b — Text-over-image contrast (Part 33)

Text placed visually over a kit illustration MUST sit inside an
`.image-overlay` wrapper carrying one of:

- `.scrim-bottom` — gradient bottom-up; use when text sits at
  the bottom of the image (most common — concert hero, lifestyle
  cover).
- `.scrim-top` — mirror; text at top.
- `.scrim-left` — horizontal gradient; text at left edge.
- `.scrim-radial` — ellipse dim under centered text on a
  photo-rich hero.

Add `.is-light-text` when the text is **light-color on a dark
photo** but the photo has bright highlights that would still
swallow it — this flips the scrim from black-to-transparent to
white-to-transparent (the scrim itself becomes light-bias,
dimming highlights toward the text color).

**Correct pattern:**

```html
<div class="layer image-overlay scrim-bottom" style="left:0; top:0; width:1920px; height:1080px;">
  <img src="../../../kit-corporate/assets/_shared/concert-hero.jpg" alt="" />
  <p
    class="overlay-text txt-hero c-white"
    style="bottom:120px; left:153.333px; max-width:1466.667px;"
  >
    Phoebe Bridgers,<br />the room you wanted.
  </p>
</div>
```

**Forbidden pattern:** bare `<img>` with absolute-positioned
text sibling, no `.image-overlay`. The text falls on whatever
luminance happens to be under it; the same layout reads on one
photo and fails on the next swap.

_Why the scrim is mandatory, not «consider it»:_ photo luminance
distribution varies per asset. A layout that tests cleanly on a
moody night-concert shot disappears on a daytime festival photo
when the photographer swaps the hero asset. The scrim is the
**property of the wrapper**, not of a specific photo — it makes
text legibility a layout invariant, not a content-dependent
gamble.

_Why direction matters:_ scrim-bottom on text-at-top wastes the
gradient (text sits on the clear part of the image while the
opaque part dims nothing). Pick by text bbox position: bottom →
`scrim-bottom`; top → `scrim-top`; horizontal edge → `scrim-left`;
centered → `scrim-radial`. Wrong direction → verify-slide.sh §
Text-over-image gate still flags as
`text_over_image_scrim_direction_missing` if the bbox doesn't
intersect the scrim's opaque zone.

_Why darken the image, don't lighten the text (Part 55):_ the
kit's text colors are fixed by `--c-*` tokens — they're a brand
decision, not a contrast workaround. Images are swappable
assets; changing text color to "fix" contrast is a fragile
patch that breaks the next time the photographer swaps the
photo. The scrim is the **only** sanctioned fix: it makes
contrast a property of the wrapper, robust to image swaps, and
keeps every slide's typography on-brand. The digital-product-poc
skill enforces the same principle for image heroes in pitch
sites (see `references/pitch-concept-site-21st.md § Image hero
& scrim`).

Verify-slide.sh § Text-over-image gate enforces the wrapper's
presence and the direction's appropriateness.

### § 0.11 — Markdown drafting markers never render in final HTML

`[weak]` (Part 9), `~~strikethrough~~`, raw `**bold**`, raw
`_italic_` — these are **drafting annotations**, never visible
content. Before materialization (Step 7), strip them entirely OR
convert to proper HTML:

| Drafting form       | Final HTML                                                |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `[weak]` line       | drop entirely OR rewrite as concrete claim                |
| `~~strikethrough~~` | drop entirely (drafting cross-out has no visible meaning) |
| `**bold word**`     | `<span class="hl-bold">bold word</span>`                  |
| `_italic word_`     | `<em>italic word</em>`                                    |

> _Why:_ the slides «weeks 1-4 / 5-7 / 8-11 / 12+» and «Clients we've
> worked with» from a real deck shipped with literal `~~text~~`
> strike-through markup in the final render. Markdown markers are for
> the model's drafting layer; the kit's typography classes are for the
> output.

### § 0.11b — No em dash in slide copy (Part 49)

The em dash `—` (U+2014) is **banned** from every slide (headlines, body,
captions, table cells, footers) — it reads as an AI writing tic. Ordinary
hyphens in compound words (`end-to-end`, `CI/CD`) are fine. Rewrite guidance
and examples live in **SKILL.md Step 6** (single source). The `em_dash_banned`
gate (`scripts/lib/slide-checks.js`) blocks any slide whose text still
contains `—`.

### § 0.12 — Background ↔ slide-type consistency

The corporate kit splits backgrounds into **title** vs **content**
pools. Using the wrong pool for a slide type reads as «background under
wrong content» — a vivid title surface behind a 3-column data slide, or
a flat content surface behind a section divider.

| Background pool             | Designed for                                                   | NEVER use with                                         |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `bg-title-03/04/05` (vivid) | Cover (03/04/05); final (03/05 — **NOT 04**)                   | content slides, section dividers, bg-title-04 on final |
| `bg-title-01/02/06` (muted) | Section dividers (one per section); `06` also `statement.html` | content slides, cover                                  |
| `bg-cover-light`            | Two-logo (partnership) cover                                   | anything else                                          |
| `bg-content-01…08`          | Content slides (one per section, reused)                       | covers, dividers, final                                |

The content backgrounds are flat light surfaces and are
**column-count-agnostic** — they carry brand identity, not panel
structure, so any `.cols-N` (N = 1–6) sits cleanly on any
`bg-content-0N`.

> _Why:_ the background pool signals the slide's role. A vivid
> `bg-title` behind body content makes the data unreadable and breaks
> the section rhythm; a flat `bg-content` behind a divider drops the
> chapter signal. Match the background pool to the slide type; pick the
> column count by the content's item count (`.cols-N`), independent of
> the background.

**Enforcement:** `scripts/verify-deck.sh` parses each slide's
background class and slide type and validates pool compatibility per
the table above. Mismatch → `escalation_flag:
background_pool_mismatch`.

### § 0.13 — Eyebrow row pattern (Part 22 unified — inline default)

All multi-column templates use `.col-eyebrow` inline flex row by default —
text + decorative line on the SAME baseline. **One pattern for everything:**
works identically for digit eyebrows ("01") and text eyebrows ("Step 01" /
"Sprint 0" / "Phase 1 · 2 weeks").

```html
<div class="col">
  <div class="col-eyebrow">
    <p class="col-num txt-body c-light-blue">01</p>
  </div>
  <p class="col-title txt-h1 is-tight c-white">Visual tokens</p>
</div>
```

The `.col-eyebrow` flex row places text on the left at its natural width;
the `::after` pseudo-element fills the column's remaining width with a 2 px
decorative line. Text + line share the same baseline.

**Variants:**

- `.col-eyebrow.is-warm` — yellow line (recommendation tone).
- `.col-eyebrow.is-coral` — red line (warning tone).

**No eyebrow at all?** Drop the `.col-eyebrow` wrapper; col-title starts at
the top of the column.

> _Why one pattern (Part 22 unify):_ Part 20 had two modes (digit-only =
> `.col-accent` above column; text = `.col-eyebrow` inline). Real decks
> showed two failure modes:
>
> 1. Agent applied BOTH `.col-accent` AND `.col-eyebrow` simultaneously
>    → double line (empty stripe above + inline-with-line below).
> 2. Digit eyebrows ("01") rendered above-line-below-digit while the
>    user expected digit-inline-with-line.
>    Inline-everywhere defaults remove the choice and the failure modes.

#### Legacy `.col-accent` — avoid

The `.col-accent` class (Mode A above-column stripe) may still exist in
[`components.css`](kit-corporate/shared/components.css) for backward
compatibility — don't replicate the pattern; use `.col-eyebrow` for any
slide.

The global default for `.col-accent` (`top: -21.333px`) still applies
if you somehow ship a `.col-accent` div — but you shouldn't. The
corporate kit's `templates/` are the canonical examples and use
`.col-eyebrow`.

### § 0.14 — Lists MUST declare bullet-icon variant (Part 26)

Every `<ul>` rendered as part of slide content MUST carry a
`.disc-list.has-icons.is-<variant>` class. Pick by semantic role
(see kit-map § 5c):

- `.is-star` — energy / benefits / capabilities / what-we-give.
- `.is-chevron` — sequential / process / next-step / journey.
- `.is-dot` — neutral fact / data / list-as-information / meta-fact
  (default for «Owner: X · Timing: Y» / «Output: Z» rows).

**Forbidden:** bare `<ul><li>…</li></ul>` without a `disc-list` /
`has-icons` / `is-*` class chain. Browser default `list-style: none` is
inherited from the layout shell in most kit contexts → result is
unmarked bare paragraphs (the «Half-day with CPO, CMO» / «Output:
aligned brief» bug from the user's deck). The bullet glyph carries
visual rhythm that connects related items; without it, the column
reads as disconnected sentences.

When the content is genuinely paragraph-shaped (label-value «Owner:
Onepark · Timing: within 2 weeks»), still wrap in
`.disc-list.has-icons.is-dot` — the dot icon serves as «this is a
meta-fact» marker AND preserves vertical rhythm against other
columns' bulleted lists.

### § 0.15 — Template materialisation migration (Part 29)

When materialising a template, you copy both its HTML structure AND any
scoped `<style>` block. **A scoped style block may encode positioning
that fights current rules.** The agent's job is to migrate the content
to current rules before integration. Otherwise the slide visually
regresses (eyebrow strikethroughs, overflowing split text, broken
bullets).

**Mandatory migration checks on every materialised slide:**

1. **Eyebrow pattern (Part 22 §0.13).** If the fork has
   `<div class="col-accent">` + `<p class="col-num">…</p>` AND the
   `.col-num` content is anything OTHER than a single digit / pure
   numeric, migrate to `.col-eyebrow` inline:

   ```html
   <!-- BEFORE (legacy fork): -->
   <div class="col-accent" style="…"></div>
   <p class="col-num">Design Lead</p>

   <!-- AFTER (Part 22 inline): -->
   <div class="col-eyebrow">
     <p class="col-num">Design Lead</p>
   </div>
   ```

   ALSO: **remove the scoped `.col-accent { top: 25.333px }` rule** from
   the fork's `<style>` block. The Part 17 global default
   (`top: -21.333px` above column) applies cleanly to digit-only fallbacks;
   the legacy `top: 25.333px` puts the line midline of text → strikethrough.

2. **Content-zone overflow (Part 29).** Content MUST fit the `content`
   zone:
   - 1-line heading → content starts at `top: 280px`; 2-line heading →
     `top: 358.667px`.
   - The content zone **always ends by `top: 930.667px`** — nothing may
     cross that line (footer sits at y985.333).
   - **Available height ≈ 488 px (1-line heading).** If your content
     exceeds this (a long heading wrapping past 2 lines + dense
     cards / list), it bleeds past y930.667 into the footer.
   - Mitigations (in order of preference):
     a. **Shorten content.** Trim the heading to ≤ 2 lines and reduce
     body copy / item count.
     b. **Pick a roomier template.** Move from a dense grid to a
     `content-split` / `content-stacked-list` layout, or fewer
     `.cols-N` columns.
     c. **Restructure** the slide into two slides if both halves are
     dense.

3. **Bullet markers (Part 26 §0.14).** Slides with `<ul><li>…</li></ul>`
   must carry `.disc-list.has-icons.is-{star,chevron,dot}` class — add
   the class on materialisation if the template ships a bare `<ul>`.

4. **Stylesheet links (Part 28).** Confirm all three `<link>` tags
   (tokens + layouts + components) are present and resolve to
   `../../../kit-corporate/shared/`. `materialize-slide.sh` handles
   this; hand-edits often drop layouts.css / components.css.

5. **HUMAN-REFINEMENT-NEEDED comments inline.** If you embed a
   `<!-- HUMAN-REFINEMENT-NEEDED: ... -->` comment inside a `<p>`
   tag, the comment counts toward the text node's rendered height
   ONLY if it contains substantial text. To be safe — emit comments
   ON A SEPARATE LINE inside `<div>`, not inside `<p>`.

**Verify gate:** `verify-slide.sh` (Part 29) detects:

- `.col-accent + .col-num text` antipattern → flags as
  `eyebrow_legacy_mode_a_misuse`.
- content-zone bottom > 930.667 → flags as `content_zone_overflow`.

Both must pass before the slide ships.

### § 0.16 — Card surface contrast pair (Part 33)

Cards use the `.card.is-light` / `.card.is-dark` variants. Each
variant carries a **parent-surface contract**:

- `.card.is-light` (white surface, dark text) MUST sit on a
  parent `.layer` whose background is **dark or saturated**:
  any `bg-title-0N` dark surface, a dark `--c-*` fill, or a kit
  illustration whose dominant region is dim / colored.
- `.card.is-dark` (dark surface, light text) MUST sit on a
  parent `.layer` whose background is **light**: any `bg-content-0N`
  light surface, paper / off-white surface, or a kit illustration whose
  dominant region is bright.

**Forbidden pattern:** four `.card.is-light` in a row on a
`bg-content-0N` light surface — the cards' white surface + decorative
dot dissolve into the light parent and the white text reads as
floating fog.

**Correct patterns:**

1. _Single-shade cards, opposite parent._ Four light cards on a
   dark parent, or four dark cards on a light parent. This is the
   default — the contract holds.
2. _Mixed-shade cards on one parent._ If the slide thesis genuinely
   requires four cards in two visual tones, **alternate per card by
   underlying parent region**: cards over the dark half of the
   parent are `.is-light`; cards over the light half are
   `.is-dark`. Use a split-layer pattern (two `bg-*` layers
   side-by-side) to give each card a defined backdrop.

The kit's `.card.is-light` / `.is-dark` ship a 6%-opacity hairline
border as **last-resort defence** — if the agent ignored the
parent-pair rule, the hairline keeps the card minimally readable.
But the hairline is the patch, not the design — the rule is the
parent-pair contract.

_Why the rule exists:_ the regression repeats on every multi-card
grid generated without parent-shade thinking — light cards on light
parents, dark cards on dark parents, white decorative dots
dissolving into white surfaces. The contract makes the agent
decide parent-shade **before** card-variant, not after; that
sequencing fixes the failure mode at the planning step instead of
patching it at the render step.

Verify-slide.sh § Card-pair contrast gate computes parent layer
luminance and flags violations as
`card_pair_contrast_violated`.

### § 0.17 — Bottom-edge padding floor (Part 34)

No content element's bounding rect may cross the **content-zone
bottom at y930.667** — the content zone ends there by convention, leaving
the band below it for the footer at y985.333. The heading band starts at
y114.667; the y930.667 floor establishes the matching bottom breathing room.

**Forbidden pattern.** A mockup / image / textbox whose bottom in
canvas coordinates ends up at > 930.667 px (the canvas is 1080 px tall, so
this leaves < 112 px of bottom breathing). Composition that pushes to
y930.667+ feels «pinned» to the edge, with no visual breathing and a
collision risk with the footer row.

**Exception.** The footer row (`.footer-tagline` / `.footer-section` /
`.page-number`) is canonically placed at y985.333 by kit convention. It's
a typographic mark, not content. Excluded from the gate.

_Why a hard floor:_ slide composition rhythm is driven by margins
as much as by content. The y86 heading band establishes a vertical
beat the eye expects; without the symmetric y930.667 bottom floor, the slide
reads bottom-heavy and pinned. The floor doesn't tell the agent
HOW to fix — it just refuses to ship slides where the bottom
ratio is broken. Fixes are usually: lift the element 40-80 px,
trim a content block, or split the slide.

Verify-slide.sh § 6.4 Bottom-edge padding gate flags violations
as `bottom_padding_violated` with the gap distance in evidence.

### § 0.18 — Bullet-list grid in narrow columns must stack vertically (Part 38)

When a bullet-list (`.disc-list` or `.disc-list.has-icons`) sits
inside a column whose **content width is ≤ 500 px**, the bullets
MUST stack vertically (one bullet per row), NOT lay out as a
2-per-row grid (`grid-cols-2`, `flex-wrap` with two siblings
sharing the same y, etc.).

**Forbidden pattern.** A four-bullet block laid out as a 2×2 grid
inside a ~450-px-wide column:

```html
<div class="col" style="width: 600px;">
  <ul class="disc-list has-icons is-star grid grid-cols-2 gap-4">
    <li>25+ years of product engineering</li>
    <li>Strategy + craft, one team</li>
    <li>Travel · fintech · consumer apps</li>
    <li>Built to ship, not just present</li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

**Why this matters.** PowerPoint Arial renders ~5–10% wider than
the Chromium screenshot's fallback font (Helvetica Neue on macOS).
Bullet text that fits comfortably on one line in HTML can overflow
into the neighbouring column in pptx — the «Travel · fintech ·
consumer apps» bullet's last word collided with the next column's
`✦ Built to ship` icon in a real regression. Vertical stacking
guarantees no horizontal collision regardless of Arial-drift,
because each row has the full column width to itself.

**Correct pattern.** Single-column stack:

```html
<div class="col" style="width: 600px;">
  <ul class="disc-list has-icons is-star">
    <li>25+ years of product engineering</li>
    <li>Strategy + craft, one team</li>
    <li>Travel · fintech · consumer apps</li>
    <li>Built to ship, not just present</li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

The 500-px threshold is calibrated against kit typography
(`.txt-body-lg` at 32 px font-size with ~5 % Arial drift = ~26 px
safety margin per row). Columns wider than 500 px have enough
slack to accommodate 2-per-row layouts even under Arial-drift.

Verify-slide.sh § 6.5 «Bullet-grid in narrow column» gate detects
violations and flags as `bullet_grid_in_narrow_column: <selector>:
<column-width-px>`.

### § 0.19 — Nowrap-slot character limits (Part 39)

Several kit components hold their text on **one line** by design —
the icon-and-text alignment relies on a single-line baseline:

| Slot                             | Selector          | Slot width                 | Char limit at kit font                                                        |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.bullet-row` p in 2×2 fact grid | `.bullet-row p`   | ~454 px                    | **≤ 26 chars at 37.333px Bold**                                               |
| `.col-eyebrow .col-num`          | `.col-num`        | varies per column          | **≤ 8 chars** (typically 2-digit nums + suffix)                               |
| `.stat-row`                      | `.stat-row`       | full layer width           | **≤ 60 chars at 28px**                                                        |
| `.slide-heading`                 | `.slide-heading`  | 1613.333 px content column | **≤ 50 chars at 64px (H3) — 1 line; longer wraps to the 2-line heading band** |
| `.footer-tagline`                | `.footer-tagline` | column / footer width      | **≤ 40 chars at 16px (P7)**                                                   |

Stock kit labels («150+ Professionals», «Modern Agile Approach»,
«25 Years of Experience», «Worldwide Presence») all sit at
~16-24 chars and fit comfortably. When the agent supplies content
through these slots, **measure the result against the limit**
before shipping.

**Why it matters.** The slot's CSS originally carried
`white-space: nowrap` to keep icon + text on one baseline. When
the supplied text exceeded the slot width, it overflowed into the
neighbouring grid cell — the «25 years of design + engineering»
fact bled into the next column's icon zone. Part 39 removed
nowrap from `.bullet-row p` so the overflow degrades to «wraps to
2 lines inside the slot» instead of «overlaps next column». This
is a **graceful fallback**, not a license to write long labels —
the fact grid was designed for short scannable copy. Long labels
break the visual rhythm even when they wrap correctly.

**Correct pattern.** Either fit the limit (preferred), or pick a
different slot (e.g. `.stat-row` for longer, `.col-title` for
non-grid contexts).

**Forbidden pattern.** Supplying 30+ char text into `.bullet-row`
and relying on either nowrap-overflow (which Part 39 fixed) or
wrap-to-2-lines (which works but looks cramped against neighbour
slots in a tight grid). The verify-slide.sh § 6.6 «nowrap-overflow»
gate catches the former; this rule's char-limit constraints catch
the latter at composition time.

Verify-slide.sh § 6.6 gate flags `nowrap_overflow: <selector>:
<text-width-px>vs<slot-width-px>` for any element whose content
overflows its slot in either nowrap-still-present or
wrap-but-still-cramped state.

---

## 1. Custom visual elements — encouraged, kit-style-locked (Part 26)

**Default bias: add visual structure when content warrants it.** Don't
ship plain content if a kit-native visual block would carry it better.
The kit's gradient panels, callout stripes, AIMS-chip labels, ghost-letter
watermarks, mega-line punch text, and persona-style illustrations are the
agent's palette — combine them freely on slides that need rhythm beyond
the bare template defaults.

**Strict constraint — kit-style adherence (every custom element must obey):**

- **Colours** from `--c-*` tokens only (no hex literals, no off-system hues).
- **Gradients** — the kit has no gradient tokens. The only gradient is the
  case-study tag, baked into `.tag.is-case-study`; vivid title backgrounds
  are raster images. Do not invent an inline gradient for a single slide.
- **Typography** from `.txt-*` classes only (no inline `font-family`, no
  ad-hoc `font-weight: 500`).
- **Shapes** composed of kit primitives — `.bg-content-*` / `.bg-title-*`
  surfaces, `.numbered-card`, `.icon-block`, `.tag.is-*`, `.divider-h` /
  `.divider-v`, `.disc-list.has-icons.is-*`. Combine, don't invent.
- **Spacing** on the kit grid — `gap-*` tokens, not arbitrary values.
- **Custom SVGs** allowed if composed of brand fills (`--c-*` only);
  existing illustrations in `kit-corporate/assets/` are first choice.

**What this license does NOT cover:**

- New typography families.
- Off-palette colours (any red that isn't `#e85b4f` coral; any blue not in
  `--c-*-blue` derivatives).
- Decorative patterns from outside the kit's visual language (photographic
  textures, skeuomorphic shadows, invented gradient meshes — the kit has no
  gradient tokens).
- Sub-objects that compete with the slide's hierarchy (oversized accents
  that out-shout the headline).

**When to add a sub-object** (default bias = YES if any apply):

- A key statistic / claim needs visual anchoring — wrap in gradient
  panel + bold mega-line.
- A section needs rhythm between two text blocks — add accent stripe,
  ghost-letter watermark, or a thin gradient divider.
- Two parallel ideas need visual contrast — AIMS-chip label left + body
  right.
- A list has 1–2 items that need extra weight — callout family
  (`.callout.is-yellow/.is-coral/.is-cool`).
- The slide is content-light and feels empty — add a kit-native
  illustration in a free canvas zone (per `references/canvas-zones.md`).

**When NOT to add:**

- The slide already has dense visual rhythm.
- Cover slides (kit handles covers; don't crowd).
- Decoration would obscure narrative meaning.
- You can't justify it in `deck_output.new_objects_introduced[]` with a
  one-line «why this slide needed it» and a kit-token attribution.

---

### Template-ladder escape — when even compose-from-primitives isn't enough

If the kit's existing primitive set genuinely doesn't contain the right
shape AFTER you've tried composing freely from the palette above, then:

1. Change the `.cols-N` count in an existing template.
2. Combine content blocks from two templates inside one canvas.
3. Swap the content background (`bg-content-0N`).
4. Swap the illustration.

If still no fit, **compose** it from existing kit primitives:

| Allowed building block                                 | What it gives you                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| `.layer`                                               | Absolutely-positioned wrapper inside `.slide` |
| `.txt-*` classes                                       | Typography — never invent a new size          |
| `.c-*` classes / `--c-*` variables                     | Brand colour                                  |
| `.flex-col` / `.flex-row` + `.gap-*`                   | Layout rhythm                                 |
| `.col-table` + `.col` + `.col-accent`                  | Multi-column tables                           |
| `.bullet-list` + `.bullet-row` + `.bullet-icon`        | Bullet patterns                               |
| `.disc-list`                                           | Disc-style lists                              |
| `.pill`                                                | Pill chips                                    |
| `.diamond-wrap` + `.diamond`                           | Diamond accents                               |
| `.browser-window` + `.browser-tabbar` + `.browser-dot` | Mock-browser frame                            |

Each new sub-object must:

- inherit typography scale (no new font sizes / families),
- inherit the colour palette (`--c-*`),
- inherit the spacing rhythm (gaps from `.gap-*`),
- carry a `data-new-object="<short-name>"` attribute for traceability,
- be documented in `deck_output.new_objects_introduced` with its name,
  slide index, purpose, list of building blocks, and the reason the kit
  was insufficient,
- not break any canonical position from `references/kit-map.md` §1.

> _Why composition-only:_ a "new" sub-object that introduces a new
> typography size or a new colour silently establishes a second visual
> system. Future decks then have to choose between the kit and the
> custom system, and the brand identity bifurcates. Composition keeps
> the visual surface area bounded.

### Soft limit

≤ **1 new sub-object per ~5 slides** on average across the deck. More
than that is a design smell — usually it means the template-fit pass
was too quick.

### What a new sub-object must **not** do

- Introduce a new font size, weight, or family.
- Introduce a new colour outside `--c-*` tokens, or invent a gradient (the
  kit has no gradient tokens).
- Replicate an existing component with cosmetic differences (just adapt
  the existing one).
- Break a canonical position from `references/kit-map.md` §1.

---

## 2. Anti-AI-signal rules

Forbidden by default — these are the tells that mark a deck as
AI-generated and lose audience trust within the first 10 seconds:

- decorative uppercase eyebrow / kicker above the section header,
- "recommended sample", "sample concept", "featured", "hot" pills above
  the title,
- generic feature-card grids with 6 identical icons (the kit's grids
  carry their own meaning — copying them as filler kills it),
- logo walls without approved real logos,
- overly long premium adjectives without proof,
- making every slide visually unique just for novelty,
- glow / blur cliché styling with no kit precedent,
- "modern SaaS" structure when the brief needs stronger narrative or
  product clarity.

> _Why a hard list:_ every entry above is something a generic LLM does
> by default when asked to "make a polished slide". The kit is strong
> on restraint — ride that signal, don't fight it.

If a draft slide hits any of the above, iterate before final output.

### First-viewport rules (cover + opening slide)

- One strong title.
- One supporting line if needed.
- One clear CTA or thesis line if needed.
- Strong imagery / framing — but only kit-approved assets.

Do **not** weaken the first impression with decorative micro-labels above
the title.

---

## 3. Motion

The kit templates have **no animation by design**. If motion is
required for a future deck (e.g. interactive walkthrough), it must be:

- transform-only — never `transition: all`,
- short — ≤ 240 ms for utility, ≤ 400 ms for narrative reveal,
- justified — focus, sequence, or reveal; never decoration,
- respectful of `prefers-reduced-motion`.

Forbidden by default:

- parallax,
- looping decorative animation,
- bouncing transitions,
- auto-rotating taglines.

> _Why a strict motion budget:_ the deck is presentation-ready, not a
> hero website. Motion eats slide-reading time and breaks the calm
> rhythm that gives the kit its presentation-grade feel.

---

## 4. Practical working rule (summary)

When in doubt:

- choose the nearest template,
- adapt copy, illustration, and accent colour within the kit's grammar,
- keep the canonical positions from `references/kit-map.md` §1
  untouched,
- compose new sub-objects only from documented tokens and components,
- apply client overlay additively via `:root` variables,
- run the verification checklist in `references/verification.md`,
- mark anything ambiguous as `weak_claim` / `human_refinement_needed` /
  `open_questions`.

Visual confidence comes from the kit. Story confidence comes from AIMS.
Both, or none.

---

## 5. Self-check gates (Part 26)

Run these grep-based gates against the deck output BEFORE Checkpoint #1.
Each is a hard pass/fail; failures must be fixed before delivery.

### § 5.1 — Bare `<ul>` gate (Part 26 § 0.14)

Every `<ul>` MUST carry `.disc-list.has-icons.is-<variant>`:

```bash
# Should return 0 lines: any line printed indicates a bare <ul>
grep -nE '<ul[^>]*>' tmp/decks/<deck>/*.html | grep -v 'disc-list[^"]*has-icons'
```

If non-zero → add `class="disc-list has-icons is-{star|chevron|dot}"`
per kit-map § 5c.

### § 5.2 — Kit-token attribution gate (Part 26 § 1)

Custom visual elements must use kit tokens only:

```bash
# Find any hex literal or raw rgb() inside slide HTML; should only match
# kit-defined tokens. Inline styles using --c-*/var() are fine.
grep -nE '#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,6}\b|rgb\(' tmp/decks/<deck>/*.html
```

Any match that ISN'T a kit-defined hex (existing in `tokens.css`) is a
foreign colour and must be replaced with a `--c-*` reference.

### § 5.3 — `deck_output.new_objects_introduced[]` completeness

For every slide with a custom visual element (gradient panel anchor,
callout strip, AIMS-chip row, ghost letter, persona pair beyond what the
template ships), `deck_output.new_objects_introduced[]` must have an
entry with: `slide_index`, `name`, `purpose`, `building_blocks`
(citing `--c-*` / `.callout.is-*` / etc.), and `data-new-object`
attribute on the element itself.
